pointers.sentence: Neither joins text: each template is compiled on its own, and nodes do the joining each time a page renders (`django/template/loader_tags.py`).
It then parses with no end tag to stop at, and everything after the tag, to the end of the file, becomes the node list of one `ExtendsNode` (`django/template/loader_tags.py:do_extends`).

What it keeps from it is `ExtendsNode.blocks`, every `BlockNode` in the list by name, found when the node is made through the node lists each node names in `Node.child_nodelists`: at any depth, but not inside a `simple_block_tag`, whose node names none (`django/template/loader_tags.py:ExtendsNode.__init__`, `django/template/base.py:Node.get_nodes_by_type`).

What it keeps from it is `ExtendsNode.blocks`, every `BlockNode` in the list by name, found when the node is made through the node lists each node names in `Node.child_nodelists`: at any depth, but not inside a `simple_block_tag`, whose node names none (`django/template/loader_tags.py:ExtendsNode.__init__`, `django/template/base.py:Node.get_nodes_by_type`).

`ExtendsNode.must_be_first` is true, and a node that must be first is refused in a node list that already holds anything but text: before `{% extends %}` may stand text and `{# … #}` comments, which make no node, but no variable and no other tag, `{% load %}` included (`django/template/base.py:Parser.extend_nodelist`).

`do_block` keeps on the parser the block names it has met and refuses one a second time in a template; `{% endblock %}` may repeat the block's name, and any other name is an error (`django/template/loader_tags.py:do_block`).
`BlockContext` holds, for each block name, a list of the `BlockNode`s of that name in one chain of templates (`django/template/loader_tags.py:BlockContext`).
When the child's tree renders, `ExtendsNode.render` does this, in order (`django/template/loader_tags.py:ExtendsNode.render`):

`Template.render` would push a new level onto the render context, which answers from its top level only ([Rendering: nodes and the render context](rendering.md)), and the parent's nodes would find no block context (`django/template/base.py:Template.render`).

Under `push_state` with `isolated_context=False` they render in the child's level, while `RenderContext.template` names the parent, against whose source an error in its nodes is reported ([Template errors and debug information](debugging.md)) (`django/template/context.py:RenderContext.push_state`).
`BlockNode.render` first asks the render context for a block context (`django/template/loader_tags.py:BlockNode.render`).
`BlockNode.super` is what `{{ block.super }}` calls (`django/template/loader_tags.py:BlockNode.super`).
`ExtendsNode.get_parent` resolves the tag's argument (`django/template/loader_tags.py:ExtendsNode.get_parent`).
A compiled `Template` is used as it is; from a backend's template (`django/template/backends/django.py:Template`) the compiled one inside is taken.
Its docstring gives the purpose: extends can work recursively without extending the same template twice (`django/template/loader_tags.py:ExtendsNode.find_template`).

The engine hands the list to each loader, and the base loader passes over a source whose `Origin` is in it, recording `"Skipped to avoid recursion"` in what it tried (`django/template/loaders/base.py:Loader.get_template`, `django/template/base.py:Origin`).

The cached loader keys a template found with a skip by its name and a hash of the skipped origins of that same name, so a template is compiled once whichever chain reaches it ([Finding a template: `Engine` and the loaders](loaders.md)) (`django/template/loaders/cached.py:Loader.cache_key`).

`construct_relative_path` reads a name that begins `"./"` or `"../"` relative to the name the current template was loaded by, so `{% extends "./base.html" %}` in `"fleet/port_detail.html"` names `"fleet/base.html"` (`django/template/loader_tags.py:construct_relative_path`).

`do_include` takes a template, compiled as a filter expression, and two options, each at most once: `"with"` and pairs written `name=value`, and `"only"` (`django/template/loader_tags.py:do_include`).
`IncludeNode.render` resolves the template each time (`django/template/loader_tags.py:IncludeNode.render`).

The `"with"` values are resolved in the including template's context, and the included template is rendered with its own `render` (`django/template/base.py:Template.render`, `django/template/base.py:PartialTemplate.render`).

With `"only"`, it is rendered with a new context that holds those values and nothing else (`django/template/context.py:BaseContext.new`).
